scenario_category: thin evidence that should not support a confident conclusion
description: A single outlet, citing one anonymous source, reports a possible CEO resignation; no other outlet corroborates and the company has no comment. Tests restraint: this should be 'unconfirmed', not escalated to 'consensus' or even mislabeled 'disputed' (there is no contradicting account, just an absence of corroboration).

event.title: Report of possible CEO resignation at Veridian Instruments
event.description: A single-sourced report suggests the CEO of Veridian Instruments may resign; uncorroborated.

articles.title: Veridian Instruments CEO may step down, source says
articles.summary: A single anonymous source says the CEO may resign; company declines to comment; no other outlet corroborates.
articles.raw_content: A person described as familiar with internal discussions at Veridian Instruments said the company's CEO may be preparing to step down in the coming months. The source did not provide a reason or timeline. A Veridian Instruments spokesperson declined to comment when reached. No other news outlet has reported on this account.

must_preserve_facts: Only one source, anonymous, makes this claim
No reason or timeline was given for the possible resignation
must_not_invent: A reason for the possible resignation (not given)
Any confirmation or denial by the company (it declined to comment, which is neither)
known_ambiguities: This claim should be tagged 'unconfirmed' — not 'consensus' (only one source exists) and not 'disputed' either (there is no second account contradicting it; it is simply uncorroborated). Mislabeling this as 'disputed' would be a status-category error, not just an overconfidence problem.
validation_notes: Only one article/source exists, so sources will have exactly one entry citing source_id 101 / article_id 101. This case specifically probes whether a model distinguishes 'disputed' (contradicted by another account) from 'unconfirmed' (simply unverified), a distinction the schema validator's enum check cannot itself enforce correctly — it only confirms the value is one of the four allowed strings.
